what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis), also called Lou Gehrig's disease. It works by helping protect the nerve cells in your brain and spinal cord from dying. It targets two pathways inside cells that are thought to contribute to the nerve damage seen in ALS, which may help slow down how quickly the disease gets worse.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a powder in a packet. Mix the entire contents of one packet into a cup with about 8 ounces (240 mL) of water. Stir well until the powder is fully dissolved before drinking. You can also give it through a feeding tube (PEG or NG tube) if needed. Take it on an empty stomach — at least 1 hour before a meal or 2 hours after a meal. Do not mix it with hot liquids. Drink or take the mixture right after preparing it.
dosing: The usual dose is ONE packet taken by mouth (or feeding tube) ONCE daily for the first 3 weeks. After 3 weeks, if you are tolerating it well, the dose increases to ONE packet TWICE daily (morning and evening). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on how you feel.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two packets at once to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store packets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep packets in the original box and protect them from heat and moisture. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use a packet if the seal is broken or if it has expired. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid mixing this medicine with hot beverages or food, as heat may affect how it works. Avoid skipping doses, as consistency is important for this medication to work best. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some may interact with this medication. If you have liver problems, make sure your doctor is aware, since one ingredient (taurursodiol/TUDCA) can affect liver function.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical help right away if you experience any of the following: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); dark urine or very light-colored stools; unusual tiredness or weakness; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your ALS symptoms seem to be getting significantly worse, or if you have any new or concerning symptoms.
when_it_works: This medicine works over time. It is not a cure for ALS, and it may not make you feel better right away. In clinical studies, it helped slow down the decline in function compared to placebo. It may take weeks to months before any benefit is noticed, and some people may not feel a noticeable difference. It is important to keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate changes.
special_populations: Kidney or Liver Problems: Use with caution. Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver disease before starting this medicine, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe to use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: This medicine has not been studied in children and is currently only approved for adults. Older Adults: No special dose adjustment is required for older adults, but talk to your doctor about any other health conditions or medicines you take.
